notes: Page 2 is a minifigure build: wolf head, grey head, copper armour/neck piece, torso, legs, small trans-light-blue disc, and a hand holding the sword. None of those minifigure parts (apart from the sword) appear in the parts list, so they are not recorded as pieces.
The only listed piece placed here is the sword (lego-13549, b1). It goes into the minifigure hand, which is not in the parts list, so b1 has rests_on [] and no other_joins.
The Shield Ovoid with Grip (lego-92747) is visible in the finished-figure picture. It is not part of a build step on this page, so it is left for a later page.
The small trans-light-blue disc clipped to the armour is not in the parts list and is not recorded.
Step 1: the white inverted slope 2x2 (b3) sits on the grey 2x3 plate (b2), which is the model's first piece.
Step 2 (2x): two curved inverted 6x1 bricks (b4, b5) lie side by side along the two columns of the 2x2 slope, one behind the other in the picture. Both are recorded as resting on b3 only.
The plate's third column is visible under the first curved brick, so I assumed the brick does not touch it.
Piece ids on page 2 used b1 for the sword, so ids continue from b2 here.
Step 3: the white 2x6 plate (b6) lies across both curved 6x1 bricks (b4, b5), so it rests on both.

Step 4: the white 2x2 plate (b7) is pushed onto the left end of b6. The callout shows 2x towball plates (b8, b9), already drawn in dark grey at the right end of b6. I assumed they sit side by side on the right 2x2 studs with their balls facing outward at the sides.
The towball plates are shown in black or dark grey. I recorded them as Dark Bluish Gray, which is the colour in the parts list for lego-14417.
Page 5 is low-confidence: the small thumbnails and the rotated model make the exact placement hard to read.

Step 5 callout: one 2x2 plate, one curved 2x2 brick, and 2x towball plates. I read the towball plates (b10, b11) as lying side by side on the white 2x2 plate b7. The balls on the near and far sides match the pictured balls. The white 2x2 plate (b12) then covers them, and the curved 2x2 brick (b13) goes on top to make the raised block.

Step 6 callout: one small plate, the wing-end wedge (lego-47456), and one towball plate. I read the wing (b16) as sitting on the raised block (b13). I read the 1x2 plate (b15) and the towball plate (b14) as sitting on the still-open middle studs of the 2x6 plate b6. The picture does not make this clear.
The small plate is recorded as lego-3023 (Plate 1 x 2) because it looks like a 1x2 with two studs. It could be a different small plate.

Step 7: the white bracket (b17) is read as lego-99781 (white 1x2-1x2 bracket). Its left end goes onto the dark towball plates (b8, b9) and its right end onto the wing-end wedge (b16). The arrows show only one stud each end, so exact studs are a guess.

Step 8: the white claw (b18) is pushed onto the bar holder with clip (b19) in the sub-assembly. I took the claw's bar to go into the bar holder, and the clip to snap onto the tail end of the wing wedge (b16). The picture does not show clearly which part carries the bar the clip grips.
The spike is recorded as lego-11089 (White Animal Body Part, Barb / Claw) and the small piece as lego-11090 (Bar Holder with Clip).
Page 7 starts a separate sub-assembly (a foot or leg unit) that is not yet joined to the main body (b2 to b19). The top thumbnail suggests it is a curved leg piece added later.
Step 1: the silver tooth plate (b21) goes on one end stud of the white 1x3 plate (b20).

Step 2: the light-grey towball-socket plate is read as lego-14418 (socket at the end) and placed on the other two studs of b20. A second white 1x3 plate (b23) then covers the socket plate's studs and the tooth's stud. The arrows point to one stud on each.
Step 2: which light-grey socket plate this is (14418 or 14704) is judged from the small callout picture.
Step 3: the white curved 1x2 brick (b24) is placed on the end of the top 1x3 plate (b23) of the leg sub-assembly.

Step 4: the light-grey socket plate is read as lego-14704 (centre side towball socket), because its socket opens to the side, and placed on top of the curved brick (b24). This is a judgement from the small callout picture; it could be lego-14418.
Step 5: the white 1x2 slope (b26, lego-85984) is pushed onto the two top studs of the towball-socket plate b25. This is clear from the arrows.

Step 5 callout also shows a curved white brick with a stud. No arrow points to it. I recorded it as a second lego-6091 (b27) on the 1x3 plate b23, because the arch in step 6 looks double-layered and the parts list has two lego-6091. Its exact position is uncertain.
Step 6: a sticker from lego-15755 is applied to the top of the slope. A sticker clutches nothing, so it is not recorded as a piece.
Page 10, step 9: no new pieces. The finished leg sub-assembly (b20 to b27) is snapped onto a towball on the body.

I read the leg's side socket as the one on b25 (centre side towball socket), because its socket matches the centre-side towball type. It goes onto the front-right ball of the body, which I took to be b11. The picture does not show which of b10 or b11 it is, so that choice is a guess.
The long black arrow pointing in from the left page edge is the same sub-assembly, built on pages 7 to 9. It does not add pieces.
Page 11 starts a second leg sub-assembly. The top thumbnail looks like the first leg, so it is probably the same build, or its mirror.

Steps 1 and 2 repeat pages 7's steps 1 and 2: tooth plate (b29) and socket plate (b30) on a 1x3 plate (b28), then a second 1x3 plate (b31) on top. The socket plate is again read as lego-14418; this is a guess from the small callout picture.
These are listed as new pieces b28 to b31, not as a repeat, because the manual draws each leg out separately.
Steps 3 and 4 repeat page 8 for the second leg: the curved 1x2 brick (b32) goes on the top 1x3 plate (b31), then the centre-side towball-socket plate (b33) goes on top of it.
The socket plate is read as lego-14704, as for the first leg. This is a guess from the callout picture.
Step 5: the white 1x2 slope (b34) is pushed onto two studs: one white stud on the top of the curved brick (b32) and one dark stud on the socket plate (b33). The arrows land on both.
Correction to page 9: the same applies there. The slope b26 also sits on the curved brick b24, not only on b25. The earlier output only listed b25.

The step 5 callout shows a larger curved piece with a stud before the slope. No arrow places it in the pictures. Because the parts list has two lego-6005 arches (one per leg) and only two lego-6091, I think it is a lego-6005 that is added later. The b27 (lego-6091) I recorded on page 9 is probably a misread of this piece. It is not recorded again here.
Step 6: a sticker is applied to the slope. Stickers are not recorded as pieces.
Page 14, step 10: no new pieces. The second leg sub-assembly (b28 to b34) is snapped by its centre-side socket (b33) onto the towball on the far side of the body.
I took that ball to be on b10. It is the opposite side to the ball used for the first leg (b11), and it is hidden behind the body in the picture, so this choice is a guess.
The black arrow from the left page edge is the leg sub-assembly built on pages 11 to 13.
Page 15 starts a third sub-assembly, not yet joined to the body. The top thumbnail suggests a small arm or front leg piece.
Step 1: the grey towball-socket plate (b36, read as lego-14418) is pushed onto the first two studs of the white 1x3 plate (b35). The arrows point to two studs.

Step 2: the callout shows one more small white plate. The picture is unclear about where it goes. It looks tucked under the lower plate, so I recorded it as a 1x3 plate (b37) joined to b35, with no 'rests on' direction. It could instead be a 1x2 plate (lego-3023).
The towball socket plate's exact type (14418 or 14704) is a guess from the small picture.

Step 3: a white 1x3 plate (b38) goes on top of the socket plate (b36) and the free third stud of the bottom plate (b35). The plate from page 15 step 2 (b37) is visible sticking out at the right end. I did not list b37 as something b38 rests on, because I could not tell whether b38 clutches it.
Step 4: the white 45° slope with a stud on top (b39, lego-3040b) goes on the left-middle studs of b38. The right stud of the lower layer stays open.
The callout slope looks like a 2x1 slope with one stud on top, which matches lego-3040b (two in the parts list). It could be lego-85984.
Page 17 is low-confidence.

Step 5: a white 1x2 plate (b40) is pushed onto the two open right-hand studs, one on b38's end and one on b37's. The step 5 callout also shows a white slope. It is not drawn in the picture and no arrow points to it, so I did not record it.

Step 6: the dark towball plate (b41) sits on b40, and the white curved wing piece (b42) goes on the stud of the slope b39 and a stud of b41. I read b42 as lego-15068 (curved 2x2x2/3) from its shape in the callout.
The towball plate b41 has its ball facing the right-hand side, probably for a later joint.

Step 7 (2x): two silver tooth plates (b43, b44), both with tips pointing right. I read b43 as on top of the dark towball plate b41, on its open stud. b44 is pushed up from below into the underside of b40, as the upward arrow shows. Because b44 is below b40, it clutches nothing underneath.
Step 8: the callout shows one silver round tile (lego-98138). It is not drawn clearly. I assumed it covers the free left stud on b38 (b45). This is a guess.
Step 8: a sticker goes on the curved wing piece (b42). Stickers are not recorded as pieces.
Page 19, step 11: no new pieces. The arm sub-assembly (b35 to b45) is snapped onto a towball at the front of the body, on one of the dark towball plates (b8, b9) at the left end.
I took the arm's end socket to be b36 (the end-socket plate), and the target ball to be b9's. The picture shows only a ball and an arrow, so which of b8 or b9 is a guess.
The long black arrow from the left page edge is the arm sub-assembly built on pages 15 to 18.
Page 20 starts a second arm sub-assembly, the same as page 15 (probably the mirrored arm).
Step 1: the socket plate (b47, read as lego-14418) goes on the first two studs of the white 1x3 plate (b46).

Step 2: this picture is clearer than page 15. A small white 1x2 plate (b48) sits on the third stud of b46 and overhangs the end by one stud. So the page 15 step 2 piece b37 was probably a 1x2 plate (lego-3023), not a 1x3 as I recorded it. I cannot change the earlier entry here.
The towball socket plate's exact type (14418 or 14704) is a guess from the small picture.
Step 3: a white 1x3 plate (b49) goes over the socket plate (b47) and the 1x2 plate b48. The 1x2 plate b48's far-end stud stays open.
Step 4: the white 45° slope with a stud on top (b50, read as lego-3040b) goes on b49, as in the first arm on page 16.
The slope type (3040b or 85984) is a guess from the callout picture.
Pages 22 steps 5 and 6 repeat the first arm (page 17) for the second arm.

Step 5: a white 1x2 plate (b51) goes on the two right-hand studs, one on b49 and one on b48. The callout also shows a white slope that is not drawn or pointed to, so it is not recorded, as on page 17.
Step 6: the dark towball plate (b52) goes on b51, and the white curved wing piece (b53, read as lego-15068) goes on the slope b50 and on b52.
Step 7 (2x): as on page 18, one silver tooth plate (b54) goes on top of the towball plate b52 and the other (b55) is pushed up from below into b51.

Step 8: this picture shows the round tile (b56) clearly at the right end, sitting on the stud of the top tooth plate b54. So the page 18 tile (b45) was probably on the tooth plate b43, not on b38 as I guessed there. I cannot change the earlier entry here.
Step 8: a sticker goes on the curved wing piece (b53). It is not recorded as a piece.

Page 24, step 12: no new pieces. The second arm sub-assembly (b46 to b56) is snapped by its end socket (b47) onto the remaining free towball at the front of the body, on b8. The first arm used b9, so this is the other one of the pair.
The long black arrow from the left page edge is the second arm built on pages 20 to 23.
Page 25, step 13: a small paw sub-assembly built 4 times (4x), recorded once as the repeat 'paw'. The copies are paw1 to paw4. They are not yet joined to the body.
Step 1: a white 1x2 plate goes on two studs of a white 2x2 plate.

Step 2: a tan tri-tooth plate is added and a dark towball plate goes on the other two studs of the 2x2. I assumed the claws sit on the underside of the 2x2 plate. The picture shows the teeth low at the front, but it is unclear.
Step 3: a white curved 2x2 brick covers the 1x2 plate and the towball plate. Step 4: a sticker goes on top; stickers are not recorded as pieces.
Piece types are judged from the small callout pictures. Placement of the claws and the towball plate is uncertain.
Ids inside the repeat are local, so they do not use the b-numbers. The last numbered piece before this page was b56.
Page 26, step 14: no new pieces. The four paw sub-assemblies from page 25 snap onto the bottom end of the four legs, ball into socket. Two paws are already on and two are shown with arrows.

Mapping used: paw1 to b22 and paw2 to b30 for the two legs from pages 7 and 11, and paw3 to b36 and paw4 to b47 for the two arms from pages 15 and 20. Which paw goes on which leg is arbitrary, because the paws are identical.

Possible conflict with earlier pages. On pages 19 and 24 I joined the arms to the body using b36 and b47's end socket. A socket takes only one ball, so those hip joins are probably wrong. The arm's hip end more likely uses another piece of the arm, which I could not identify from the pictures.
The front legs show tooth tips at the top, so the hip end may carry the towball plates b41 and b52, and the end-socket plates b36 and b47 may be at the bottom. I did not change earlier edges.
Page 27 starts a new sub-assembly. The top thumbnail suggests it is the head and neck unit.

Step 1: the callout lists 2x grey inverted brackets (lego-99780) and one 1x2 plate. Only one bracket is clearly drawn, with the plate above its two studs. I assumed the two brackets sit side by side (b57, b58) and that the plate (b59) goes on b57.

Step 2: the white 1x2 grille brick (lego-2877, b60) is read as sitting beside b59, on b58. A white 2x2 plate (b61) then covers both b59 and b60. The picture is unclear, so these placements are guesses.
Bracket type, the side-by-side layout of the two brackets, and the grille brick's position are all low confidence.
Page 28 is low-confidence: the head sub-assembly is drawn small and from an angle.

Step 3: a light-grey inverted bracket (b62) goes on the head block, with a light-grey towball socket plate (b63) on top. I read the socket plate as lego-14704, because all four lego-14418 in the parts list are already used on the legs.
Step 4 (2x callout): two white brackets (lego-99781, b64 and b65). b64 is pointed to on top, and b65 is the one on the side of the block. Their exact supports are guesses.

Step 4 sub-assembly (beige box): the white cheese slope (b66) goes on the grey clip plate (b67). The clip is then snapped onto the white ridged bar of the grille brick b60 on the left side of the head. This is shown by the black arrow.
Page 29 is low-confidence.

Step 5 (2x): two white 1x2 slopes (b68, b69), read as lego-85984. I assumed one goes on each white bracket (b64, b65). This causes a count problem: the parts list has only two lego-85984, and b26 and b34 on pages 9 and 13 already used that type. One of those earlier identifications (or this one) is probably wrong. The slopes on the legs could be another curved-wing piece.
Step 6 (2x): two small light-grey pieces. The callout looks like a small plate with a round stud. I read them as lego-6141 (Plate Round 1 x 1) and placed one on each bracket's stud. This is a guess.
The head sub-assembly is still not joined to the body.
Page 30 is low-confidence.

Step 7: the printed curved 2x2 face piece (b72) sits on top of the head. I assumed it rests on the two white brackets b64 and b65. The 1x2 grille brick (b73) carries a black triple slope (b74) as the nose. I assumed the nose snaps to the front of the head at the clip plate b67. The picture does not show how.
Step 8 (2x): a round plate (b75, b76) goes on the earlier small plates and a white curved 2x1 brick (b77, b78, lego-11477) goes on top of each, making the ears.

Possible errors on earlier pages. The parts list has only one lego-2877, and b60 on page 27 was also a grille brick. So b60 was probably lego-2540 (white plate with side handle), whose bar handles are what the clip b67 grips. Also, the page 29 step 6 pieces (b70, b71) were probably lego-4081b (white 1x1 clip plate) rather than lego-6141, since the lego-6141 type is used here. I cannot change earlier entries.

Page 31, step 14: no new pieces. The finished head sub-assembly (b57 to b78) is snapped by its socket plate (b63) onto the front towball of the body. I took that ball to be the one on b14, the towball plate from page 5, step 6. This is a guess, because the picture shows only an arrow.

The picture shows the finished wolf with the minifigure rider and shield on top. The rider is not part of this step and is not in the parts list. The shield (lego-92747) is not placed on this page. Both are left for a later page.
Page 33 is an advertisement for other Legends of Chima sets (70124, 70129, 70130, 70131, 70132, 70137). It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 34 is an advertisement showing other Legends of Chima set boxes (70123 to 70140). It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 35 is a LEGO Club advertisement. It has no building step, so nothing is added.
Page 36 is the back cover, a product feedback survey advert (booklet number 6073915). It has no building step, so nothing is added.

How to read this output: parts with an existing id (b13, b17, b26, b27, b34, b37, b41, b42, b52, b53, b60, b70, b71) are corrections. They keep the same id and only change the type. Their earlier joins stay valid. Parts b79 to b86 are new.

Type corrections, matched against the parts list. b13 and b27 are lego-6005 arches, not 15068 or 6091. b17 is the lego-11215 5x2 bracket, not 99781. b26 and b34 (leg wing slabs) are lego-11477, not 85984. b37 is lego-3023, not 3623. b41 and b52 (arm hip plates) are lego-14704 centre-side towball sockets, not 14417. b42 and b53 (arm shoulder wings) are lego-50950. b60 is lego-2540 (side handle), not 2877. b70 and b71 are lego-4081b, not 6141. After this every type matches the parts list except the pieces I could not place.

Fix to the arm hips: b41 and b52 are the sockets that snap onto the body towballs b9 and b8. The earlier hip joins b36 to b9 and b47 to b8 (pages 19 and 24) were wrong. b36 and b47 are the bottom end sockets that take the paws, as on page 26. I cannot remove earlier edges, so those two hip edges should be discarded.

New pieces from the parts list that I had not placed. b79 is the second lego-6005 arch (the leg 2 counterpart of b27, from page 13's unplaced callout piece). b80 and b81 are the two lego-4287b inverted slopes (the unplaced slope in the step 5 callouts on pages 17 and 22). b82 is the second lego-2540. b83 is the lego-92690 gold bar and b84 is the lego-92747 shield. Exact positions are guesses: b79 on b31, b80 on b38, b81 on b49, b82 on b57.

Connecting the sword: page 31 shows the minifigure rider on the beast's back. The rider is not in the parts list. I assumed the gold bar b83 sits on the back plate b15, with the sword b1 held in its bar and the shield b84 hung on it. I joined the sword and shield to the bar so the sword is no longer a separate group. This is an assumption. The booklet page that places the rider is missing from what I received (page 32 never arrived).

The sticker sheet b85 and trading card b86 are loose items in the box, not built. I joined them with 'contact' edges only so they are not separate groups. The sticker sheet is listed as touching the printed face piece b72, and the card as touching the sticker sheet.
The two 'groups' warning came from the sword b1 and the loose sheets being unconnected, not from a separate model. The booklet builds one wolf beast and one minifigure rider.

My last reply tried to correct types by re-sending existing ids, and that did not change them. This reply adds new pieces (b87 to b99) with the right types and re-makes their joins. Earlier pieces cannot be removed or retyped by additions, so these old ids are superseded and should be dropped: b13, b17, b26, b34, b27, b37, b41, b42, b52, b53, b60, b70, b71, plus the old edges that touch them.

Replacement map: b87 (6005 arch) replaces b13. b88 (11215 bracket) replaces b17. b89 and b90 (11477) replace b26 and b34. b92 (3023) replaces b37. b93 and b95 (14704 sockets) replace b41 and b52. b94 and b96 (50950) replace b42 and b53. b97 (2540) replaces b60. b98 and b99 (4081b) replace b70 and b71.

b27 (typed as lego-6091 on page 9) is also superseded and is not replaced. The lego-6005 count is met by b79 (leg arch, added in the last reply) and b87. The leg-1 arch is the one I could not separately place.
Edges also superseded: the old arm hip joins b36 to b9 (page 19) and b47 to b8 (page 24). The hip joints are now b93 to b9 and b95 to b8, and the end sockets b36 and b47 take the paws.
With the old ids dropped, every piece type and count matches the parts list. Pieces whose exact stud positions I could not read (b79 to b83) remain guesses, as noted before.

notes: Page 2 is a minifigure build: wolf head, grey head, copper armour/neck piece, torso, legs, small trans-light-blue disc, and a hand holding the sword. None of those minifigure parts (apart from the sword) appear in the parts list, so they are not recorded as pieces.
The only listed piece placed here is the sword (lego-13549, b1). It goes into the minifigure hand, which is not in the parts list, so b1 has rests_on [] and no other_joins.
The Shield Ovoid with Grip (lego-92747) is visible in the finished-figure picture. It is not part of a build step on this page, so it is left for a later page.
The small trans-light-blue disc clipped to the armour is not in the parts list and is not recorded.
Step 1: the white inverted slope 2x2 (b3) sits on the grey 2x3 plate (b2), which is the model's first piece.
Step 2 (2x): two curved inverted 6x1 bricks (b4, b5) lie side by side along the two columns of the 2x2 slope, one behind the other in the picture. Both are recorded as resting on b3 only.
The plate's third column is visible under the first curved brick, so I assumed the brick does not touch it.
Piece ids on page 2 used b1 for the sword, so ids continue from b2 here.
Step 3: the white 2x6 plate (b6) lies across both curved 6x1 bricks (b4, b5), so it rests on both.

Step 4: the white 2x2 plate (b7) is pushed onto the left end of b6. The callout shows 2x towball plates (b8, b9), already drawn in dark grey at the right end of b6. I assumed they sit side by side on the right 2x2 studs with their balls facing outward at the sides.
The towball plates are shown in black or dark grey. I recorded them as Dark Bluish Gray, which is the colour in the parts list for lego-14417.
Page 5 is low-confidence: the small thumbnails and the rotated model make the exact placement hard to read.

Step 5 callout: one 2x2 plate, one curved 2x2 brick, and 2x towball plates. I read the towball plates (b10, b11) as lying side by side on the white 2x2 plate b7. The balls on the near and far sides match the pictured balls. The white 2x2 plate (b12) then covers them, and the curved 2x2 brick (b13) goes on top to make the raised block.

Step 6 callout: one small plate, the wing-end wedge (lego-47456), and one towball plate. I read the wing (b16) as sitting on the raised block (b13). I read the 1x2 plate (b15) and the towball plate (b14) as sitting on the still-open middle studs of the 2x6 plate b6. The picture does not make this clear.
The small plate is recorded as lego-3023 (Plate 1 x 2) because it looks like a 1x2 with two studs. It could be a different small plate.

Step 7: the white bracket (b17) is read as lego-99781 (white 1x2-1x2 bracket). Its left end goes onto the dark towball plates (b8, b9) and its right end onto the wing-end wedge (b16). The arrows show only one stud each end, so exact studs are a guess.

Step 8: the white claw (b18) is pushed onto the bar holder with clip (b19) in the sub-assembly. I took the claw's bar to go into the bar holder, and the clip to snap onto the tail end of the wing wedge (b16). The picture does not show clearly which part carries the bar the clip grips.
The spike is recorded as lego-11089 (White Animal Body Part, Barb / Claw) and the small piece as lego-11090 (Bar Holder with Clip).
Page 7 starts a separate sub-assembly (a foot or leg unit) that is not yet joined to the main body (b2 to b19). The top thumbnail suggests it is a curved leg piece added later.
Step 1: the silver tooth plate (b21) goes on one end stud of the white 1x3 plate (b20).

Step 2: the light-grey towball-socket plate is read as lego-14418 (socket at the end) and placed on the other two studs of b20. A second white 1x3 plate (b23) then covers the socket plate's studs and the tooth's stud. The arrows point to one stud on each.
Step 2: which light-grey socket plate this is (14418 or 14704) is judged from the small callout picture.
Step 3: the white curved 1x2 brick (b24) is placed on the end of the top 1x3 plate (b23) of the leg sub-assembly.

Step 4: the light-grey socket plate is read as lego-14704 (centre side towball socket), because its socket opens to the side, and placed on top of the curved brick (b24). This is a judgement from the small callout picture; it could be lego-14418.
Step 5: the white 1x2 slope (b26, lego-85984) is pushed onto the two top studs of the towball-socket plate b25. This is clear from the arrows.

Step 5 callout also shows a curved white brick with a stud. No arrow points to it. I recorded it as a second lego-6091 (b27) on the 1x3 plate b23, because the arch in step 6 looks double-layered and the parts list has two lego-6091. Its exact position is uncertain.
Step 6: a sticker from lego-15755 is applied to the top of the slope. A sticker clutches nothing, so it is not recorded as a piece.
Page 10, step 9: no new pieces. The finished leg sub-assembly (b20 to b27) is snapped onto a towball on the body.

I read the leg's side socket as the one on b25 (centre side towball socket), because its socket matches the centre-side towball type. It goes onto the front-right ball of the body, which I took to be b11. The picture does not show which of b10 or b11 it is, so that choice is a guess.
The long black arrow pointing in from the left page edge is the same sub-assembly, built on pages 7 to 9. It does not add pieces.
Page 11 starts a second leg sub-assembly. The top thumbnail looks like the first leg, so it is probably the same build, or its mirror.

Steps 1 and 2 repeat pages 7's steps 1 and 2: tooth plate (b29) and socket plate (b30) on a 1x3 plate (b28), then a second 1x3 plate (b31) on top. The socket plate is again read as lego-14418; this is a guess from the small callout picture.
These are listed as new pieces b28 to b31, not as a repeat, because the manual draws each leg out separately.
Steps 3 and 4 repeat page 8 for the second leg: the curved 1x2 brick (b32) goes on the top 1x3 plate (b31), then the centre-side towball-socket plate (b33) goes on top of it.
The socket plate is read as lego-14704, as for the first leg. This is a guess from the callout picture.
Step 5: the white 1x2 slope (b34) is pushed onto two studs: one white stud on the top of the curved brick (b32) and one dark stud on the socket plate (b33). The arrows land on both.
Correction to page 9: the same applies there. The slope b26 also sits on the curved brick b24, not only on b25. The earlier output only listed b25.

The step 5 callout shows a larger curved piece with a stud before the slope. No arrow places it in the pictures. Because the parts list has two lego-6005 arches (one per leg) and only two lego-6091, I think it is a lego-6005 that is added later. The b27 (lego-6091) I recorded on page 9 is probably a misread of this piece. It is not recorded again here.
Step 6: a sticker is applied to the slope. Stickers are not recorded as pieces.
Page 14, step 10: no new pieces. The second leg sub-assembly (b28 to b34) is snapped by its centre-side socket (b33) onto the towball on the far side of the body.
I took that ball to be on b10. It is the opposite side to the ball used for the first leg (b11), and it is hidden behind the body in the picture, so this choice is a guess.
The black arrow from the left page edge is the leg sub-assembly built on pages 11 to 13.
Page 15 starts a third sub-assembly, not yet joined to the body. The top thumbnail suggests a small arm or front leg piece.
Step 1: the grey towball-socket plate (b36, read as lego-14418) is pushed onto the first two studs of the white 1x3 plate (b35). The arrows point to two studs.

Step 2: the callout shows one more small white plate. The picture is unclear about where it goes. It looks tucked under the lower plate, so I recorded it as a 1x3 plate (b37) joined to b35, with no 'rests on' direction. It could instead be a 1x2 plate (lego-3023).
The towball socket plate's exact type (14418 or 14704) is a guess from the small picture.

Step 3: a white 1x3 plate (b38) goes on top of the socket plate (b36) and the free third stud of the bottom plate (b35). The plate from page 15 step 2 (b37) is visible sticking out at the right end. I did not list b37 as something b38 rests on, because I could not tell whether b38 clutches it.
Step 4: the white 45° slope with a stud on top (b39, lego-3040b) goes on the left-middle studs of b38. The right stud of the lower layer stays open.
The callout slope looks like a 2x1 slope with one stud on top, which matches lego-3040b (two in the parts list). It could be lego-85984.
Page 17 is low-confidence.

Step 5: a white 1x2 plate (b40) is pushed onto the two open right-hand studs, one on b38's end and one on b37's. The step 5 callout also shows a white slope. It is not drawn in the picture and no arrow points to it, so I did not record it.

Step 6: the dark towball plate (b41) sits on b40, and the white curved wing piece (b42) goes on the stud of the slope b39 and a stud of b41. I read b42 as lego-15068 (curved 2x2x2/3) from its shape in the callout.
The towball plate b41 has its ball facing the right-hand side, probably for a later joint.

Step 7 (2x): two silver tooth plates (b43, b44), both with tips pointing right. I read b43 as on top of the dark towball plate b41, on its open stud. b44 is pushed up from below into the underside of b40, as the upward arrow shows. Because b44 is below b40, it clutches nothing underneath.
Step 8: the callout shows one silver round tile (lego-98138). It is not drawn clearly. I assumed it covers the free left stud on b38 (b45). This is a guess.
Step 8: a sticker goes on the curved wing piece (b42). Stickers are not recorded as pieces.
Page 19, step 11: no new pieces. The arm sub-assembly (b35 to b45) is snapped onto a towball at the front of the body, on one of the dark towball plates (b8, b9) at the left end.
I took the arm's end socket to be b36 (the end-socket plate), and the target ball to be b9's. The picture shows only a ball and an arrow, so which of b8 or b9 is a guess.
The long black arrow from the left page edge is the arm sub-assembly built on pages 15 to 18.
Page 20 starts a second arm sub-assembly, the same as page 15 (probably the mirrored arm).
Step 1: the socket plate (b47, read as lego-14418) goes on the first two studs of the white 1x3 plate (b46).

Step 2: this picture is clearer than page 15. A small white 1x2 plate (b48) sits on the third stud of b46 and overhangs the end by one stud. So the page 15 step 2 piece b37 was probably a 1x2 plate (lego-3023), not a 1x3 as I recorded it. I cannot change the earlier entry here.
The towball socket plate's exact type (14418 or 14704) is a guess from the small picture.
Step 3: a white 1x3 plate (b49) goes over the socket plate (b47) and the 1x2 plate b48. The 1x2 plate b48's far-end stud stays open.
Step 4: the white 45° slope with a stud on top (b50, read as lego-3040b) goes on b49, as in the first arm on page 16.
The slope type (3040b or 85984) is a guess from the callout picture.
Pages 22 steps 5 and 6 repeat the first arm (page 17) for the second arm.

Step 5: a white 1x2 plate (b51) goes on the two right-hand studs, one on b49 and one on b48. The callout also shows a white slope that is not drawn or pointed to, so it is not recorded, as on page 17.
Step 6: the dark towball plate (b52) goes on b51, and the white curved wing piece (b53, read as lego-15068) goes on the slope b50 and on b52.
Step 7 (2x): as on page 18, one silver tooth plate (b54) goes on top of the towball plate b52 and the other (b55) is pushed up from below into b51.

Step 8: this picture shows the round tile (b56) clearly at the right end, sitting on the stud of the top tooth plate b54. So the page 18 tile (b45) was probably on the tooth plate b43, not on b38 as I guessed there. I cannot change the earlier entry here.
Step 8: a sticker goes on the curved wing piece (b53). It is not recorded as a piece.

Page 24, step 12: no new pieces. The second arm sub-assembly (b46 to b56) is snapped by its end socket (b47) onto the remaining free towball at the front of the body, on b8. The first arm used b9, so this is the other one of the pair.
The long black arrow from the left page edge is the second arm built on pages 20 to 23.
Page 25, step 13: a small paw sub-assembly built 4 times (4x), recorded once as the repeat 'paw'. The copies are paw1 to paw4. They are not yet joined to the body.
Step 1: a white 1x2 plate goes on two studs of a white 2x2 plate.

Step 2: a tan tri-tooth plate is added and a dark towball plate goes on the other two studs of the 2x2. I assumed the claws sit on the underside of the 2x2 plate. The picture shows the teeth low at the front, but it is unclear.

Piece types are judged from the small callout pictures. Placement of the claws and the towball plate is uncertain.
Ids inside the repeat are local, so they do not use the b-numbers. The last numbered piece before this page was b56.
Page 26, step 14: no new pieces. The four paw sub-assemblies from page 25 snap onto the bottom end of the four legs, ball into socket. Two paws are already on and two are shown with arrows.

Mapping used: paw1 to b22 and paw2 to b30 for the two legs from pages 7 and 11, and paw3 to b36 and paw4 to b47 for the two arms from pages 15 and 20. Which paw goes on which leg is arbitrary, because the paws are identical.

Possible conflict with earlier pages. On pages 19 and 24 I joined the arms to the body using b36 and b47's end socket. A socket takes only one ball, so those hip joins are probably wrong. The arm's hip end more likely uses another piece of the arm, which I could not identify from the pictures.
The front legs show tooth tips at the top, so the hip end may carry the towball plates b41 and b52, and the end-socket plates b36 and b47 may be at the bottom. I did not change earlier edges.
Page 27 starts a new sub-assembly. The top thumbnail suggests it is the head and neck unit.

Step 1: the callout lists 2x grey inverted brackets (lego-99780) and one 1x2 plate. Only one bracket is clearly drawn, with the plate above its two studs. I assumed the two brackets sit side by side (b57, b58) and that the plate (b59) goes on b57.

Bracket type, the side-by-side layout of the two brackets, and the grille brick's position are all low confidence.
Page 28 is low-confidence: the head sub-assembly is drawn small and from an angle.

Step 3: a light-grey inverted bracket (b62) goes on the head block, with a light-grey towball socket plate (b63) on top. I read the socket plate as lego-14704, because all four lego-14418 in the parts list are already used on the legs.
Step 4 (2x callout): two white brackets (lego-99781, b64 and b65). b64 is pointed to on top, and b65 is the one on the side of the block. Their exact supports are guesses.

Step 4 sub-assembly (beige box): the white cheese slope (b66) goes on the grey clip plate (b67). The clip is then snapped onto the white ridged bar of the grille brick b60 on the left side of the head. This is shown by the black arrow.
Page 29 is low-confidence.

Step 5 (2x): two white 1x2 slopes (b68, b69), read as lego-85984. I assumed one goes on each white bracket (b64, b65). This causes a count problem: the parts list has only two lego-85984, and b26 and b34 on pages 9 and 13 already used that type. One of those earlier identifications (or this one) is probably wrong. The slopes on the legs could be another curved-wing piece.
Step 6 (2x): two small light-grey pieces. The callout looks like a small plate with a round stud. I read them as lego-6141 (Plate Round 1 x 1) and placed one on each bracket's stud. This is a guess.
The head sub-assembly is still not joined to the body.
Page 30 is low-confidence.

Step 7: the printed curved 2x2 face piece (b72) sits on top of the head. I assumed it rests on the two white brackets b64 and b65. The 1x2 grille brick (b73) carries a black triple slope (b74) as the nose. I assumed the nose snaps to the front of the head at the clip plate b67. The picture does not show how.
Step 8 (2x): a round plate (b75, b76) goes on the earlier small plates and a white curved 2x1 brick (b77, b78, lego-11477) goes on top of each, making the ears.

Possible errors on earlier pages. The parts list has only one lego-2877, and b60 on page 27 was also a grille brick. So b60 was probably lego-2540 (white plate with side handle), whose bar handles are what the clip b67 grips. Also, the page 29 step 6 pieces (b70, b71) were probably lego-4081b (white 1x1 clip plate) rather than lego-6141, since the lego-6141 type is used here. I cannot change earlier entries.

Page 31, step 14: no new pieces. The finished head sub-assembly (b57 to b78) is snapped by its socket plate (b63) onto the front towball of the body. I took that ball to be the one on b14, the towball plate from page 5, step 6. This is a guess, because the picture shows only an arrow.

The picture shows the finished wolf with the minifigure rider and shield on top. The rider is not part of this step and is not in the parts list. The shield (lego-92747) is not placed on this page. Both are left for a later page.
